title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
keyIdea: addWord is a normal trie insert. search is a DFS over the pattern: a letter follows its link; a '.' tries every existing child and returns true as soon as one leads to a full match. At the end of the pattern, return the node's flag.

approaches.name: List of words, compare each
approaches.idea: Store words in a vector; search compares the pattern with every word of the same length.
approaches.why: Every search may look at every stored word.

approaches.name: Trie + DFS for dots
approaches.idea: dfs(index, node): end → flag; '.' → try all children; letter → follow its link or fail.
approaches.time: addWord O(L); search O(L) without dots, up to O(26^d · L) with d dots
approaches.why: Letters follow one path; each dot can branch into up to 26 children (LeetCode allows at most 2 dots).

quiz.q: What does a '.' in the pattern do in the DFS?
options: Tries every existing child, one after another

quiz.q: Why return true as soon as one child succeeds?
options: One full match is enough; the other branches don't matter

quiz.q: After addWord("bad"), what does search("ba") return?
options: false: the path exists but no word ends at "ba"

quiz.q: Why is search slower with many dots?
options: Each dot can branch into up to 26 children, multiplying the paths to try

steps: What can the pattern contain? How many dots at most? What does a dot match?
Add bad, dad, mad. Work out search .ad and b.. by hand on the trie.
Store words in a list and compare: time per search?
"Prefix structure + wildcard": what changes compared to a plain trie search?
What are the DFS parameters? What happens at a dot, at a letter, at the end?
Code it, saying "letter follows one link, dot tries all, end returns flag".
